key_insight: ExpectileGCN learns how to aggregate graph neighborhoods beyond the mean, capturing class-relevant distributional differences, especially in heterophilic graphs.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive aggregation may improve node classification and robustness when connected nodes differ in class or graph inputs are corrupted.
method: Learn an expectile level that shifts aggregation between minimum- and maximum-type behavior, with the mean as a special case.
Use sigmoid smoothing and fixed-point iterations for differentiable, end-to-end training.
Analyze stability, transductive generalization, and classification risk under heterophilic neighborhood models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive performance and improved robustness to feature corruption and structural perturbations on homophilic and heterophilic benchmarks, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Fixed-point aggregation introduces iterative computation; its convergence behavior and runtime overhead should be assessed in deployment.
paper_title: Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation
